meta.subtitle: How the 40 computers in an Audi e-tron talk to each other — and to you

buses.label: CAN
buses.why: The workhorse. Multicast with priority arbitration — enough for slow comfort signals.

buses.label: CAN FD
buses.why: CAN extended: bigger payload (up to 64 B) and faster — for dense powertrain and HV traffic.

buses.label: FlexRay
buses.why: Deterministic and redundant: every message has a fixed time slot, so a brake command always arrives in time.

buses.label: LIN
buses.why: One wire, a few cents. For tiny actuators where CAN would be overkill.

buses.label: Automotive Ethernet
buses.why: Bandwidth for camera/radar data, maps and diagnostics. DoIP runs here.

topology.note: The gateway sits on every bus, so it is never listed as a bus member. FlexRay and Ethernet are drawn as stars centred on the gateway; CAN and CAN FD as shared lines; LIN hangs off its master, not the gateway.

harness.basis: Schematic routing along the usual MLB evo paths: dash cross-car beam, firewall pass-throughs, front-end carrier, sills, centre tunnel, A/B-pillar door boots and the rear wheelhouses. Not traced on the car.

scenarios.title: Select D and pull away
scenarios.blurb: Shift-by-wire, torque requests to both axles, and high-voltage power out of the pack.

steps.caption: The gear selector is just a sensor. It sends a gear request over CAN FD to the Vehicle Control Unit.
The VCU decides how much torque each axle gets and asks the battery for power — three commands on the powertrain CAN FD.
Power, not data: HV DC leaves the pack, the inverters turn it into 3-phase AC and the motors turn.
The pack reports state of charge back to the VCU, which tells the cluster what to draw as energy flow (BAP) — crossing from CAN FD to CAN through the gateway.

scenarios.title: Unlock and open the doors
scenarios.blurb: One body computer commands four door modules, the lamps and the tailgate.

steps.caption: Body Control Module 1 sends lock / window commands to all four door modules on the comfort CAN.
Coming-home lighting: BCM1 drives the Matrix-LED modules over CAN; BCM2 reaches the rear lights over LIN, the slowest wire in the car.
Tailgate open — another BCM1 command on the same CAN.
Finally the cluster is told, over BAP, which doors are open so it can draw them.

scenarios.title: Plug in and charge
scenarios.blurb: The charger, the pack and the thermal system negotiate while the cluster keeps score.

steps.caption: The VCU hands the on-board charger its charge schedule over CAN FD.
Charge power flows into the pack while thermal management asks the BECM to condition the cells — the thermal command crosses from CAN to CAN FD.
The BECM reports state of charge, cell voltages and temperatures; the cluster gets the battery state (BAP).

scenarios.title: Five radars, one picture
scenarios.blurb: Perception runs on Ethernet into the zFAS, which feeds the rest of the car.

steps.caption: The long-range radar and the two front corner radars stream detections over Automotive Ethernet to the zFAS.
The two rear radars do the same. Ethernet is a switched star: every stream passes the switch at the gateway.
The zFAS publishes one fused environment model to the gateway and the assistance status to the cluster.

scenarios.title: A tester reads the cluster
scenarios.blurb: The exact path the inventory scan took: laptop → OBD → gateway → ECU → back.

steps.caption: The laptop opens a DoIP connection (TCP 13400) through the OBD socket. It can only ever talk to the gateway.
The gateway rewrites the logical address and forwards 22 F187 onto the comfort CAN, to the cluster.
The cluster answers 62 F187 4KE920795D; the gateway routes the reply back out. Repeat forty times and you have the inventory.
